ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $O$ is the midpoint of the diagonal $BD$ of rectangle $ABCD$, and $E$ is the midpoint of side $AB$. Given that $AB = 12$ and $OE = \frac{5}{2}$, what is the length of segment $OC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since quadrilateral ABCD is a rectangle, \\
$\therefore$$\angle$A=$\angle$BCD=$90^\circ$, DO=OB,\\
since E is the midpoint of side AB,\\
$\therefore$OE is the median of $\triangle$ADB, OE=$\frac{5}{2}$,\\
$\therefore$AD=$2$OE=$5$,\\
since AB=$12$,\\
$\therefore$BD=$\sqrt{AD^{2}+AB^{2}}=\sqrt{12^{2}+5^{2}}=13$,\\
since O is the midpoint of the diagonal BD of rectangle ABCD,\\
$\therefore$OC=$\frac{1}{2}$BD=$\boxed{\frac{13}{2}}$.

method.method_draft: Right-triangle/circumcenter route: From the image, read that AB is horizontal, E lies midway on AB, O is vertically above E on the drawn segment OE, and O connects to B through diagonal DB and to C through segment OC. From the text, E is the midpoint of AB, so EB=AB/2=6, and OE=5/2. In triangle OEB, OE is perpendicular to AB because OE joins the midpoints of AB and DB in triangle ABD, so it is parallel to AD, and AD is perpendicular to AB in the rectangle. Therefore triangle OEB is right, giving OB=sqrt(EB^2+OE^2)=sqrt(6^2+(5/2)^2)=13/2. Since O is the midpoint of one diagonal of a rectangle, it is the rectangle center; the center is equidistant from all vertices, so OC=OB=13/2.

Reasoning: Using the coordinate method, let A=(0,0), B=(12,0), D=(0,h), C=(12,h). Because E is the midpoint of AB, E=(6,0). Because O is the midpoint of BD, O=((12+0)/2,(0+h)/2)=(6,h/2). Thus OE is the vertical distance from (6,0) to (6,h/2), OE=h/2. Given OE=5/2, so h/2=5/2, obtaining h=5. Therefore O=(6,5/2), C=(12,5). OC=sqrt((12-6)^2+(5-5/2)^2)=sqrt(6^2+(5/2)^2)=sqrt(36+25/4)=sqrt(169/4)=13/2.
